S57.01.needs: a signed-in account in Cloud mode; the Web search row appears only when the mobile release enables it
S57.01.note: Search row label comes from the display map; the toggle is hidden when FEATURES.webSearch is off.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Assistant > Capabilities.
Under AGI Cloud, check the Web search row is on (its value reads Cloud).
Go back to a Cloud chat and ask about a recent event or today's news.
Look for a Search the web row in the reply and tap it to expand.
Compare with Expected: the search and its sources (1 source or N sources, with links) should be shown.
S57.01.where: Settings > Assistant > Capabilities > Web search (then a Cloud chat)

S57.02.needs: a Cloud account; a public web page address
S57.02.note: The success label Web Fetch is not a literal in the code; it comes from the readable-name rule in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-display.ts. No separate on/off control for fetch was found.
steps: Open a Cloud chat (Settings > Assistant > Capabilities shows Cloud mode).
Paste a full web page address and ask what the page says.
Look for a tool row in the reply; a row named Web Fetch (generated from the tool name web_fetch) should appear.
If the fetch fails, the row reads Failed to fetch: followed by the address; compare with Expected.
S57.02.where: Cloud chat: paste a web page address and ask what it says

S57.03.note: Rollout flag in packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json:161 is server-only, and no source-reader tool control was found in apps/mobile. The only source control found is the Open source link on search results (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/WebSearchResultCard.tsx), which is not a document reader.

S57.04.needs: a Cloud chat with files available to the account
S57.04.note: Searched for search_files and open_file: found in apps/web/lib/server/tools/file-tool-names.ts and the web tool loop, but no mobile control or visible label was found in apps/mobile.

S57.05.needs: a Cloud account with code execution enabled on the server
S57.05.note: Only the sandbox gate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20) and the Code execution and file creation row (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/capabilities/index.tsx) were found; no file-read tool name or phone control was located. Plan says the server switch AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 is needed.

S57.06.needs: a Cloud account with code execution enabled on the server
S57.06.note: Same as S57.05: only the sandbox gate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20) was found; no file-write tool name or phone control was located.

S57.07.needs: a Cloud account; the Code execution and file creation row must not show Off
S57.07.note: Row shows Off when FEATURES.codeExecution is false in this release. Download artifact is an accessibility label, not confirmed as printed text.
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Capabilities and check Code execution and file creation is not Off.
In a Cloud chat, ask for a spreadsheet (for example a three-month budget in Excel format).
When the file card appears in the reply, tap it to open the file.
Tap the download control (Download artifact) and confirm an .xlsx file can be opened or shared, as Expected says.
S57.07.where: Settings > Assistant > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation, then a Cloud chat that asks for a spreadsheet

S57.08.needs: a Cloud account; the Code execution and file creation row must not show Off
S57.08.note: Same gate as S57.07. The file type is chosen by the model, not by a phone control.
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Capabilities and check Code execution and file creation is not Off.
In a Cloud chat, ask for a Word document (docx) on a topic.
When the file card appears, tap it to open the document.
Tap the download control (Download artifact) and confirm a .docx file opens or can be shared.
S57.08.where: Settings > Assistant > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation, then a Cloud chat that asks for a Word document

S57.09.needs: a Cloud account; the Code execution and file creation row must not show Off
S57.09.note: Same gate as S57.07. The file type is chosen by the model, not by a phone control.
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Capabilities and check Code execution and file creation is not Off.
In a Cloud chat, ask for a short presentation (pptx) on a topic.
When the file card appears, tap it to open the deck.
Tap the download control (Download artifact) and confirm a .pptx file opens or can be shared.
S57.09.where: Settings > Assistant > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation, then a Cloud chat that asks for a slide deck

S57.10.needs: a Cloud account; the Code execution and file creation row must not show Off
S57.10.note: Run again only appears when the tool is terminal and the conversation allows it.
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Capabilities and check Code execution and file creation is not Off.
In a Cloud chat, ask for a short Python program that prints a result (for example the first ten square numbers).
Look for a Run code row in the reply and tap it to expand.
Check the Code heading shows the code and the Output heading shows the printed result.
Optionally tap Run again under the code and compare the new output with Expected.
S57.10.where: Settings > Assistant > Capabilities > Code execution and file creation, then a Cloud chat with a Run code row

S57.12.needs: a Cloud account with code execution enabled on the server
S57.12.note: Only the sandbox gate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20) was found; no patch or edit tool name or phone control was located in apps/mobile.

labels.text: Allow eligible Cloud chats to create generated images.

S57.16.needs: a Cloud account; the Image generation row must be on (eligible chats only)
S57.16.note: The image card is rendered for image.v1 cards in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/InteractiveCardBlock.tsx.
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Capabilities and check the Image generation row is on (its value reads Cloud).
Go back to a Cloud chat and ask for a picture (for example a lighthouse at dusk).
Look in the reply for the generated image card.
Compare with Expected: the image should appear in the transcript.
S57.16.where: Settings > Assistant > Capabilities > Image generation, then a Cloud chat

S57.17.needs: a Cloud chat with an image to change
S57.17.note: Image-card rendering is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/InteractiveCardBlock.tsx, but no phone control to supply or attach an image for editing was found, and the edit tool name was not located.

labels.text: Account memories used in Cloud chats.

S57.21.needs: a Cloud account (memory is used in Cloud chats)
S57.21.note: Memory tool row names (Save Memory, Search Memory, Forget Memory) are generated from save_memory, search_memory and forget_memory (apps/web/lib/server/tools/memory-tools.ts), not literal strings.
steps: Open Settings > Assistant > Memory and note what is listed.
In a Cloud chat, type: Remember that my favourite colour is green.
Look for a memory tool row in the reply and tap it to expand if it has details.
Go back to Settings > Assistant > Memory and check the new fact is listed; then ask the chat to forget it and check it is removed.
S57.21.where: Settings > Assistant > Memory, then a Cloud chat

S57.22.needs: a phone with calendar access granted and some events on the day
S57.22.note: Expected names a Google Calendar connector, which is not set up (plan says the owner must create the OAuth client); only the phone's own calendar tools (Read your calendar, Check your availability, Add to your calendar) were found.
steps: Open Settings > Device > Permissions and confirm calendar access is allowed for the phone.
In a chat, ask: What is on my calendar today?
Look for a Read your calendar row in the reply and tap it to expand.
Compare the events shown with your phone Calendar app, as Expected says.
S57.22.where: Settings > Device > Permissions (calendar access), then a chat that asks about your calendar

S57.23.note: Searched apps/mobile for Slack and messaging tool names: no match. The Connectors page (Settings > Cloud > Connectors, apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx) exists, but no messaging tool or Slack entry was located in the phone code.

S57.24.needs: a plan that includes scheduled tasks (the screen says Scheduled tasks require Basic on lower plans)
S57.24.note: Only create_schedule exists as a chat tool (apps/web/lib/server/tools/schedule-tool.ts); listing and deleting schedules happen on the Schedules screen, not through a chat tool.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules.
Tap Create Schedule, enter a name, the prompt and how often it runs, then save.
Check the new schedule appears in the Schedules list and is active.
Optionally, in a Cloud chat ask for a reminder schedule and look for the create tool row.
S57.24.where: Schedules > Create Schedule (from the side menu), and the create_schedule tool in a Cloud chat

S57.26.needs: a Cloud chat (the assistant decides when to ask)
S57.26.note: The card is rendered for clarify.v1 cards in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/InteractiveCardBlock.tsx.
steps: In a Cloud chat, send a vague request that needs choices, for example: Help me plan a trip.
Look for a card with questions and options in the reply.
Pick an option, or type in the Something else box, then tap Send answers.
Check the assistant continues using your answer, as Expected says.
S57.26.where: Cloud chat: a question card with choices and a Send answers button

S57.28.note: Tool discovery is server-side: apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts and tool-schema-loader.ts. No phone control or visible label was found.
S57.28.where: no screen; the effect is only in what the model answers

S57.29.note: Server-side tool search exists (apps/web/lib/connectors/tool-search.ts, tool-schema-loader.ts). No user-facing tool search control in apps/mobile was found, so the user-side part of Expected could not be located.

S57.31.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
S57.31.note: A row can be tapped only when it has arguments or output.
steps: In a Cloud chat with Web search on, ask a question that needs a web search.
Tap the Search the web row to expand it.
Look under the Request heading for the query or the arguments the tool was called with.
Compare with Expected: the arguments (query, command, file or JSON) are shown.
S57.31.where: Any tool row in a chat (for example Search the web): tap the row

S57.32.needs: a Cloud account with Web search on
S57.32.note: No running elapsed-time display was found in ToolCallTimeline.tsx; the duration chip appears only after completion.
steps: In a Cloud chat with Web search on, ask a question about current events.
While the search runs, watch the row: it reads the running form (for example Searching the web…) with a shimmer.
When it finishes, the row changes to Searched the web and a duration chip appears.
Compare with Expected: an elapsed-time counter while running is not in the code; only the duration after it finishes.
S57.32.where: Any running tool row in a Cloud chat (for example Search the web)

S57.33.needs: a Cloud account with a finished tool call
S57.33.note: The preview is the expanded Response text; no separate short-preview truncation was found for small results.
steps: In a Cloud chat with Web search on, ask a question that needs a web search.
Look at the finished row's right side for a short chip (a duration or a results count).
Tap the row and read the text under the Response heading.
Compare with Expected: a short preview of the result is shown.
S57.33.where: Any finished tool row in a Cloud chat: tap it, then read the Response heading

S57.34.needs: a Cloud account with a finished tool call
S57.34.note: View full output appears only for large results (more than 12 lines or a large size).
steps: In a Cloud chat, run a tool (for example a web search) and wait until the row is finished.
Tap the row; the chevron turns down and the Request and Response sections appear.
Tap the row again to collapse it.
For a long result, tap View full output to open the full-screen sheet, then close it and compare with Expected.
S57.34.where: Any tool row in a Cloud chat: tap to expand, tap again to collapse

S57.36.needs: a Cloud account with code execution enabled
S57.36.note: The large-result reference and store are server-side (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-result-store.ts, tool-loop.ts); only the phone full-output sheet is visible to the user.
steps: In a Cloud chat with code execution on, ask for a program that prints many lines (for example 100 numbers).
Tap the Run code row to expand it.
Tap View full output to open the complete result in a full-screen sheet.
Compare with Expected: the full text is kept and can be opened later; the context reference itself is server-side and not visible.
S57.36.where: A long tool result in a Cloud chat: expand the row, then tap View full output
